newsitem.title: USA: Signet to sell 39 branches, take charge, cut jobs.
newsitem.headline: Signet to sell 39 branches, take charge, cut jobs.

text.p: Signet Banking Corp. said on Tuesday it would sell 39 branches and take a $57 million charge under a restructuring plan launched last October.

The branch sale will result in a loss of 165 jobs, bringing the net job loss under the restructuring to 327, or 7.5 percent of its total work force. However, the southeastern banking company said the program is expected to add $10 million to revenues and reduce expenses by $58 million, or 72 cents a share, by the end of 1998.
The Richmond, Va.-based bank said that in addition to the pre-tax charge, to be taken in the second quarter, it would buy back up to 5 percent of its stock by the end of the year.

The company did not give estimates for its earnings or revenues for the quarter, and a spokeswoman declined to make projections. After the changes are completed over the next 18 months, however, the company will "achieve significantly increased profitability," Chairman Malcom McDonald said in a statement.
Signet said the branch sale will affect outlets located in Southwest Virginia, the Northern Neck of Virginia and the Eastern Shore of Virginia and Maryland.

While 1,135 positions have been eliminated since October, it said actual employee impact will be considerably less because 808 positions were reduced without layoffs -- 311 by a hiring freeze, 156 by voluntary separations, 176 by projected attrition and 165 by the proposed sale of branches.
